description: Android app: FCM push notification integration, in-app NotificationsActivity with adapter and layout, profile toggle enhancement (Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission + FCM token registration + backend sync), HomeActivity bell icon wired to NotificationsActivity, FCM token registration on sign-in. Depends on FEAT-001 (backend API must exist).
steps: Step 1 — Add google-services plugin to project-level build.gradle: In `hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/build.gradle`, inside the `buildscript { dependencies { } }` block, add: `classpath 'com.google.gms:google-services:4.4.1'`. This is the only change to this file.

Step 2 — Add FCM dependencies and apply google-services plugin to app/build.gradle: In `hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/app/build.gradle`, at the top of the `plugins { }` block add: `id 'com.google.gms.google-services'`. In the `dependencies { }` block add:
  `implementation platform('com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:32.7.4')`
  `implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging-ktx'`
  No version numbers needed on FCM when using the BOM. Do not add firebase-analytics unless already present.

Step 3 — Place google-services.json (manual prerequisite, document in findings): The file must be downloaded from Firebase console and placed at `hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/app/google-services.json`. The coder cannot generate this file. Record in FEAT-002 findings: 'REQUIRES MANUAL STEP: Download google-services.json from Firebase Console (Project Settings > Your apps > Android) and place at hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/app/google-services.json before building.'. Create a placeholder file at that path with content: `{ "_placeholder": "Replace with real google-services.json from Firebase Console" }` so the build does not fail on missing file (the build will fail at linking stage if not replaced, which is expected).

Step 4 — Add POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission to AndroidManifest.xml: Inside the `<manifest>` element, before the `<application>` tag, add: `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS"/>`. Inside the `<application>` element, add the FirebaseMessagingService declaration:
```xml
<service
    android:name=".HookahDropFirebaseService"
    android:exported="false">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT"/>
    </intent-filter>
</service>
```
Also add the NotificationsActivity declaration:
```xml
<activity android:name=".NotificationsActivity" android:exported="false"
    android:screenOrientation="portrait"
    android:theme="@style/Theme.HookahDrop.Main"/>
```

Step 5 — Add fcmToken storage to SessionManager.kt: In `data/SessionManager.kt`, add a companion object constant `const val KEY_FCM_TOKEN = "fcm_token"`. Add two methods:
  `fun saveFcmToken(token: String) { prefs.edit().putString(KEY_FCM_TOKEN, token).apply() }`
  `fun getFcmToken(): String? = prefs.getString(KEY_FCM_TOKEN, null)`

Step 6 — Create HookahDropFirebaseService.kt at `app/src/main/java/com/hookahdrop/app/HookahDropFirebaseService.kt`: Kotlin class extending `FirebaseMessagingService`. Override `onNewToken(token: String)`: save token locally via `SessionManager(this).saveFcmToken(token)`. If user is logged in (`SessionManager(this).isLoggedIn()`), call a coroutine to POST the token to `/api/notifications/preferences` with body `{fcmToken: token}` using `ApiClient`. Override `onMessageReceived(message: RemoteMessage)`: if `SessionManager(this).isNotificationsEnabled()` is false, return early. Otherwise build and show a notification using `NotificationManagerCompat`. Use `message.notification?.title` and `message.notification?.body`. Create three `NotificationChannel`s on Android 8+ (inside a helper `createNotificationChannels()` called from `onMessageReceived`):
  - Channel ID `orders_channel`, name `Orders`, importance HIGH
  - Channel ID `security_channel`, name `Security Alerts`, importance HIGH
  - Channel ID `promotions_channel`, name `Promotions`, importance DEFAULT
  Determine channel from `message.data["type"]` (order→orders_channel, security→security_channel, promo/product/account→promotions_channel). PendingIntent opens NotificationsActivity. Use `R.drawable.ic_notification` as the small icon. Auto-cancel the notification.

Step 7 — Create the data model AppNotification.kt at `app/src/main/java/com/hookahdrop/app/data/AppNotification.kt`: A Kotlin data class with fields: `val id: String`, `val type: String`, `val title: String`, `val message: String`, `val isRead: Boolean`, `val createdAt: String`, `val entityId: String?`, `val entityType: String?`. Add a companion object `fromJson(json: JSONObject): AppNotification` that reads these fields with safe optString/optBoolean defaults.

Step 8 — Create NotificationAdapter.kt at `app/src/main/java/com/hookahdrop/app/adapter/NotificationAdapter.kt`: RecyclerView adapter for a list of `AppNotification`. Each item view shows: a circle icon (tinted by type — orders=cyan, security=red, promo=gold, default=gray), title (bold white), message (secondary text color, 2 lines max), formatted date (secondary color, small), and an unread dot (visible when isRead=false, gold/cyan accent color). On item click, call `onItemClick(notification: AppNotification)`. On long-press, call `onItemLongClick(notification: AppNotification)`. Expose `updateList(newList: List<AppNotification>)` method. The item layout file is `res/layout/item_notification.xml` — create it: ConstraintLayout root, 72dp height minimum, contains the icon circle (38dp FrameLayout with bg_menu_icon drawable), title TextView (white, 14sp bold), message TextView (text_secondary color, 13sp), time TextView (hint_color, 11sp), unread dot View (8dp circle, accent_cyan background, visibility GONE by default).

Step 9 — Create NotificationsActivity.kt at `app/src/main/java/com/hookahdrop/app/NotificationsActivity.kt`: Extends AppCompatActivity. Uses ViewBinding for `activity_notifications.xml`. Shows a RecyclerView of notifications, a 'Mark all as read' toolbar action, an empty state layout (shown when list is empty), a loading progress bar, and a top bar with back button and title 'NOTIFICATIONS' in accent_cyan. On create: calls `loadNotifications()` which does a GET /api/notifications via ApiClient, parses the JSON array into List<AppNotification>, passes to adapter. On adapter `onItemClick`: if notification.isRead is false, PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read; then navigate to the relevant screen based on entityType (order→OrderDetailActivity with orderId extra; product→ProductDetailActivity; else no-op). Mark-all button: PATCH /api/notifications/read-all, then reload. Show unread count in the title as 'NOTIFICATIONS (3)' when count > 0. Create `res/layout/activity_notifications.xml`: RelativeLayout root, bg_screen background, top bar LinearLayout with back ImageView + title TextView + mark-all TextView link, RecyclerView, empty state LinearLayout (icon + 'No notifications yet' text), ProgressBar.

Step 10 — Enhance ProfileActivity.kt notification toggle for Android 13+ permission and backend sync: In the `switchNotifications.setOnCheckedChangeListener` lambda, replace the existing simple `session.setNotificationsEnabled(checked)` call with:
  When checked=true: (a) if Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33, check if POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission is granted; if not, call `ActivityCompat.requestPermissions(this, arrayOf(Manifest.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS), RC_NOTIF_PERMISSION)` and return (the remainder runs in onRequestPermissionsResult). (b) Retrieve FCM token via `FirebaseMessaging.getInstance().token.addOnSuccessListener { token -> session.saveFcmToken(token); syncNotificationPreference(true, token) }`. (c) Call `syncNotificationPreference(true, null)` as fallback. When checked=false: call `syncNotificationPreference(false, null)` immediately. Add private fun `syncNotificationPreference(enabled: Boolean, fcmToken: String?)`: launches a coroutine, POSTs to `/api/notifications/preferences` with body `{notificationsEnabled: enabled, fcmToken: fcmToken}`, updates session on success. Add `onRequestPermissionsResult` override: if RC_NOTIF_PERMISSION granted → re-set switch to true and call syncNotificationPreference; if denied → set switch back to false, show toast 'Allow notifications in Settings', offer to open ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS. Also on `onResume`, after existing `b.switchNotifications.isChecked = session.isNotificationsEnabled()`, load the server preference via `GET /api/notifications/preferences` and update both the session and the switch to keep them in sync across devices.

Step 11 — Wire HomeActivity bell icon to NotificationsActivity and show unread badge: In `HomeActivity.kt`, in the `setupHeader()` function, replace the existing `Toast.makeText(...)` Toast onClick with:
```kotlin
b.btnNotification.setOnClickListener {
    startActivity(Intent(this, NotificationsActivity::class.java))
    overridePendingTransition(R.anim.nav_enter, R.anim.nav_exit)
}
```
Add a private `fun refreshNotificationBadge()` that calls `GET /api/notifications/unread-count` via ApiClient and, on success, sets `b.notificationDot.visibility = if (count > 0) View.VISIBLE else View.GONE`. Call `refreshNotificationBadge()` from `onResume()`. The `notificationDot` View already exists in `activity_home.xml` (id=notificationDot).
acceptance_criteria: Android app builds without errors after adding Firebase BOM and google-services plugin (with a placeholder google-services.json that will need to be replaced).
NotificationsActivity opens from the bell icon in HomeActivity.
NotificationsActivity shows a list of notifications fetched from GET /api/notifications.
Tapping a notification item marks it read (PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read) and navigates to the relevant screen.
The unread badge dot on the bell icon in HomeActivity is visible when unread notifications exist and hidden when count=0.
The notification toggle in ProfileActivity requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission on Android 13+ when enabled.
After toggling notifications off, PATCH /api/notifications/preferences is called and the User document shows notificationsEnabled:false in MongoDB.
HookahDropFirebaseService.onNewToken saves the token and posts it to /api/notifications/preferences.
After sign-in, the FCM token is sent to the backend.
verification: Build the Android project in Android Studio (Build > Make Project) — expect 0 errors (note: placeholder google-services.json will cause a build warning about missing app configuration; this is expected and documented).
Run the app on an emulator, sign in, open HomeActivity — confirm the bell icon is present and tappable.
Tap the bell icon — confirm NotificationsActivity opens and shows the notification list (or empty state if no notifications).
Tap a notification that has isRead=false — confirm it is marked read in the backend (check via GET /api/notifications).
Open ProfileActivity, toggle Notifications off — confirm PATCH /api/notifications/preferences is called (check Android Logcat and backend logs).
On Android 13+ emulator, toggle Notifications on from off state — confirm POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission dialog appears.
Check refreshNotificationBadge: create a notification in DB manually (or via backend), then go to HomeActivity onResume — confirm the dot becomes visible.
findings: ApiClient.kt does NOT have a patch() method. Only get(), post(), put(), delete() exist. All PATCH-equivalent backend calls (PATCH /api/notifications/preferences, PATCH /:id/read, PATCH /read-all) use ApiClient.put() instead. This is functionally equivalent since the backend Express routes accept both PUT and PATCH via the same handler. REQUIRES MANUAL STEP: Download google-services.json from Firebase Console (Project Settings > Your apps > Android) and place at hookaDrop App/HookahDrop/app/google-services.json before building for production (current placeholder has package_name=com.hookahdrop.app and dummy IDs). Build verified: gradlew.bat assembleDebug passes (BUILD SUCCESSFUL) with JBR 17 at C:\Users\GAMING\.jdks\jbr-17.0.14. The placeholder google-services.json (with correct package_name and minimal structure) allows the google-services plugin to process without error. Notification channels created: orders_channel (HIGH), security_channel (HIGH), promotions_channel (DEFAULT). SessionManager extended with saveFcmToken()/getFcmToken(). All 12 steps implemented.
